aspects.says: A plain long or double may be read and written as two 32-bit halves; a volatile one is read and written whole.
basis: section:volatile Makes Each Read and Each Write Atomic, Never a Read Followed by a Write

aspects.says: Re-checking a volatile field before writing, or applying a computed difference with addAndGet, leaves a read followed by a write and loses or misapplies updates.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: a Top-Up That Undoes a Call

aspects.says: Values that must agree go into one immutable object, built completely and published by one volatile write; two volatile fields let a reader see a new value with an old one.
basis: section:volatile Covers One Field: Values That Must Agree Are Swapped as One Immutable Object

aspects.says: Without volatile or another happens-before edge, the JIT may read a plain field once, so a loop on a flag set by another thread may never end; volatile makes every read see the latest write.
basis: section:Without volatile, a Reader May Never See the Write: the JIT May Read a Plain Field Once

aspects.says: A volatile write publishes the writes its thread made before it; writes made after it, such as filling an object already assigned to the field, are not published.
basis: section:A Volatile Write Publishes What Was Written Before It, Not What Comes After

aspects.says: Each read of a volatile field can see a new value, so a decision that uses the value more than once reads the field once into a local.
basis: section:Every Read of a volatile Field Can See a New Value: Read It Once per Decision

aspects.says: A volatile reference does not make the object or array it points to volatile; writes inside it are plain writes.
basis: section:volatile Covers One Field: Values That Must Agree Are Swapped as One Immutable Object

aspects.says: volatile makes each read and each write atomic but never a read followed by a write; an update computed from the current value needs an atomic class's updateAndGet or compareAndSet, or a lock.
basis: section:volatile Makes Each Read and Each Write Atomic, Never a Read Followed by a Write
section:Spot the Problem: a Top-Up That Undoes a Call
